subject: Banking
title: Debt-to-Income Ratio
description: A quick, practical guide to Debt-to-Income Ratio.

hook.text: Your debt-to-income ratio tells a lender how much of your paycheck already goes to debt.

buildup.text: DTI is calculated by dividing monthly debt payments by gross monthly income. A $6,000 income with $2,400 in debt is 40%.

discovery.text: Lenders use DTI because credit scores don't show income. A high score with high debt-to-income still means risk.

twist.text: Student loan payments inflate DTI for young borrowers.

climax.text: DTI is the second gatekeeper after credit score. Both must pass for approval.

punchline.text: Keep debt below 43% of income. Both score and DTI must pass.

quiz.question: What DTI ratio typically disqualifies you from a mortgage?
